answer.rationale:
The two declining metrics (activation -6%, onboarding completion -4%) point at the funnel itself, not at price, so I am spending the slot on simplify_onboarding rather than reacting to the competitor's entry pricing. memory_73 is the cautionary case: promotional_pricing bought +31% activations and +18% revenue but cost 12pp of renewal retention in exactly the SMB tier under attack, and the record explicitly says not to generalise it. Matching a discount would buy the same borrowed activation and lose the same durable revenue, against a primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_31 and memory_86 — the two memories my chosen action rests on — rather than on the ones I am rejecting. Both are compressed summaries reporting only top-of-funnel wins ('durable lift in first-week activation', 'improved completion rates and time-to-value'). Neither says anything about renewal, retention, or revenue quality downstream. That silence is the same shape as the memory_73 summary would have had if its caveat had been dropped in consolidation: an activation win with the cost stripped out. I want the original records to tell me (a) whether retention and qualified-revenue effects were measured at all or simply not carried forward, (b) how long the follow-up window was, since a 'durable' first-week lift measured over weeks says nothing about renewal, and (c) which fields were cut, because removing signup fields can mechanically raise activation while degrading lead qualification and routing — a real mechanism by which this action could shrink qualified revenue even as the dashboard improves.

Alternatives considered: activation_messaging (memory_91) is a close second and would be my fallback if verification shows memory_31/86 were confounded or measured only at the surface; it also addresses the activation drop, though it does not touch onboarding completion. referral_incentive (memory_57) targets established customers and does not address either declining metric. enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is credible but aimed at a segment that is not the one bleeding.

Running as a standard experiment with a randomised holdout, not a broad rollout: the inherited evidence supports direction but not magnitude, and prior conditions differ (day 24/52 evidence, now a competitor actively skimming price-sensitive SMBs, which changes the mix of who converts). Success is not activation lift alone — I am pre-registering retention at first renewal and qualified-revenue-per-signup as guardrails, and treating an activation gain paired with degraded lead quality as a failed test. If verification returns records that never measured beyond week one, I will treat the two memories as one weak signal rather than two independent confirmations and drop to a small guarded test.
